scenes.text: What color is a mirror? You probably think it's silver, or maybe it has no color at all because it just reflects everything.
But you’ve been lied to because perfect mirrors don't exist, and the glass used to make them actually contains tiny traces of green-tinting iron.
This means when light hits the surface, it absorbs a tiny fraction of green light instead of reflecting everything perfectly.
You can prove this yourself by placing two mirrors facing each other to create an infinite, distinctly green tunnel of reflections.
